newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN DOLLAR ENDS UP ON C.BANK, TIGHT LIQUIDITY.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN DOLLAR ENDS UP ON C.BANK, TIGHT LIQUIDITY.

text.p: The central bank's determination to ease the Taiwan dollar slide and a liquidity squeeze in the banking system pushed the local unit to a firmer close on Tuesday, reversing Monday's downtrend, dealers said.
The local unit, which fell to an intra-day low of T$28.765, reversed its earlier fall to end at T$28.718 against Monday's T$28.728 finish.
Turnover through dealers was heavy at US$331.5 million.
Dealers said the U.S. dollar's recovery in overseas markets triggered greenback buying in the morning, particularly from local importers.
"The central bank did not wait too long to halt the Taiwan dollar's slide. At noon, the Taiwan dollar firmed to T$28.719," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
A tight liquidity in the banking system also helped strengthen the Taiwan dollar, dealers said.
At 0800 GMT, the overnight interbank rate stood at above nine percent, sharply higher than the central bank's previously declared 5.50-5.5 percent target zone.
A range of T$28.65-80 was seen for Wednesday.
